Hi Amit — great to meet you earlier. Adding the quickstart and answers below; attaching a short quickstart PDF and sample payloads JSON (see attachments).

Quickstart (Hosted API eval) — summary steps:
1) Sandbox API key: aditya will provision a scoped API key for your org (14-day eval). Key-level rate limits start at 200 requests/min by default; we can bump to 1,200 requests/min for the eval if you need burst testing.
2) Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions (model param: redwood-2-small or redwood-2-medium for cost/latency comparisons).
3) Example curl:
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","prompt":"Summarize the following", "max_tokens":256}'

4) Concurrency & rate guidance: our Hosted API enforces both per-key rate limits (requests/min) and a soft concurrency limit (default 20 concurrent inflight requests per key). For eval: we can provision a higher concurrency pool (up to 100 concurrent) and a temporary higher rate limit to simulate 200 QPS bursts — note that concurrency and QPS interplay with batching and latency.
5) Cost visibility: per-request token accounting is available in the Console (token-level breakdown) and via the usage API endpoint /v1/usage. We'll share a short sample billing/estimation script in the attached sample-payloads.json.
6) Compliance: SOC2 report and data retention docs (redwood-soc2.pdf, retention-policy.html) are in the drive link Aditya included below; I'll also copy these to your secure bucket if needed.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf, sample-payloads.json

Next steps I suggest:
- Aditya: provision sandbox key for amit@finlytics.com and priya@finlytics.com.
- Amit: run the sample payloads overnight and share any failing prompts or latency outliers.
- Marissa/Neha: we (Neha) will be available for a 30-min technical sync after your initial tests (can do Thu or Fri).

Let me know what time works for the follow-up tech sync.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

1) You mentioned default concurrency of 20 concurrent requests per key; if we request 100 concurrent for the eval, will we be charged differently or see different batching behavior that would change latency numbers?
2) For the rate limit bump to simulate 200 QPS bursts, do we need to throttle on our side or will Redwood queue/batch to respect the 95th pctl latency target?

If you can confirm these two items briefly, we'll kick off tonight.

 Amit
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Singh <amit@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-26T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: Hosted API evaluation & next steps

Hi Amit — quick answers:

1) Concurrency bump: For the eval we can increase your concurrency to 100 with no change to pricing during the trial. Note that higher concurrency may increase batching efficiency which can improve token cost per request but can slightly increase tail latency for very short requests. We'll log the config for the eval so you can see exact numbers in the Console.

2) Rate-limit/200 QPS bursts: we'll provision a higher requests/min bucket to let you run 200 QPS bursts. Redwood will accept bursts up to that limit; however, to measure real-world tail latency you should run the burst from your infrastructure (so network egress and client-side concurrency are realistic). If you want, Neha can add lightweight client-side load guidance (sample locust script) to the sample-payloads.json.

I'll provision the sandbox key this afternoon and send the credentials in a separate secure email. Following that, let's tentatively lock Thu 04/29 9:30am PT for a 30-min tech sync with Neha.

Best,
Aditya
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
